#4305. The Best Commander For Each Three-Color Combination In MTG

We argue that three-colors is the sweet spot for a deck in Magic: The Gathering's Commander format. You're not too limited by having only one or two card pools to draw from, but you're also not overwhelmed, as can happen with some WUBRG Commander deck builds. That's not to say that building mono, dual, 4C, or WUBRG decks is a bad idea, but for most players, three colors is the sweet spot.

So, with that in mind, we're going to look at the single best Commander in all of MTG right now for each three-color combination with no restrictions, meaning Partner Commanders and Universes Beyond cards are included.

Updated on Friday, November 6, 2026, by Niall Walsh: This article was over two years old, so we've dived back in and brought it up to date with new selections for virtually every mana combination.

Esper holds the prestige of having the most popular Commander in all of Magic: The Gathering right now. Y'shtola, Night's Blessed has more than double the total decks created of the next most popular Esper Commander, according to EDHREC, and while Hashaton, Scarab's Fist is a great card, it requires a bit more nuance to play around.

Y'shtola, Night's Blessed is a four-mana 2/4 with Vigilance, and if any player has lost four or more life at the end of each turn, you draw a card. Then, whenever you cast a noncreature spell with a mana value of three or greater, Y'shtola deals two damage to each player, and you gain two life.

This means most Y'shtola decks will be mostly noncreature spells, with just a few creatures to support the strategy and protect you from more aggressive players.

We've seen a lot of complaints about Y'shtola, from the fact that she's a Final Fantasy / Universes Beyond card or the fact that the abilities and structure of the card are just so straightforward that it makes it very easy to play around, but ultimately, all that matters is that this card is hugely popular and by far and away the best Esper Commander in the game right now.

Take a trip through the best white, blue, and black legendary creatures (or eligible Planeswalkers) worthy of leading your next Commander deck.

From one Universes Beyond Commander to another, Sauron, the Dark Lord is a six-mana Grixis Commander who enters play as a 7/6. He also has a Ward that requires opponents to sacrifice a legendary artifact or legendary creature in order to target him with spells. Whenever an opponent casts a spell, you Amass Orcs 1, and whenever an Army you control deals combat damage to a player, the Ring tempts you. Finally, whenever the Ring tempts you, you may discard your hand, and if you do, you draw four cards.

It's safe to say that there is a damn good reason why Sauron is a hugely popular card right now, and the Commander precon he leads is among the most expensive on the market that isn't in some way limited in availability. While he may be a little limited in that you're going to want to predominantly build LotR and The Hobbit cards around it to get the most out of Sauron, he's still fun to play with.

The gap between first and second for Grixis Commanders is much smaller; however, with yet another Universes Beyond card, Fire Lord Azula, sitting in second place, we could see this Avatar card overtaking Sauron before long.

Spacecrafts have just come back around again thanks to Star Trek, but if you're looking for the best Jund Commander right now, it's Hearthhull, the Worldseed. When this four-mana Spacecraft reaches Station 2+, you ca pay one mana and tap it to sacrifice a land and draw two cards, but you may then play an additional land this turn.

When it reaches 8+ Station counters, it becomes a 6/7 with Flying, Vigilance, and Haste, and whenever you sacrifice a land, each opponent loses two life.

This card has a ton of value for only four mana, but most players get caught out by how quickly you can station it to become a creature and use both abilities. If you can crack that code and understand that Spacecrafts don't suffer from any kind of summoning sickness when still an artifact, that should help you plan your tactics, and the Haste Hearthhull gains at 8+ counters removes any requirement to wait to attack with it, too.

Up next is Pantlaza, Sun-Favored, the current leader of all Naya Commanders, although the top five Commander options for this color combination are closer than in any other category. Pantlaza is a five-mana 4/4, and the card states that whenever Pantlaza or another Dinosaur enters the battlefield under your control, you may Discover X, where X is that creature's toughness. However, you can only do this once per turn.

Discovery is a mechanic that lets you exile cards off the top of your library until you exile a nonland card with that mana value or less, which in this case is X (the creature's toughness), and you can cast that nonland card for free or put it into your hand while the other cards go on the bottom of your library in a random order.

Dino decks are extremely dangerous and feature a ton of high-power creatures that can often enter with Trample, and even if they don't, there are countless ways to grant it. There's still a lot of love for big stompy decks, and this dino Commander is head and shoulders above the rest right now.

Group hug decks are back in fashion, and one of the main drivers behind this is Ms. Bumbleflower, a four-mana Bant Commander who enters play as a 1/5 with Vigilance.

Whenever you cast a spell, target opponent draws a card. You then put a +1/+1 counter on target creature, and it gains flying until the end of the turn. If this is the second time the ability has resolved in a turn, you then draw two cards.

You're going to be pretty political when playing with Ms. Bumbleflower, as you negotiate with players who get the added card draw while you steadily build up your board presence. When the time is right, you can turn on a dime and start swinging tall and wide with creatures to try and finish off your opponents, who have hopefully been focusing on each other while you built your creatures up. You'll want plenty of protection spells to maintain your board presence, and plenty of instant spells to punish players who break any agreements at the table.

While it's a very meme-y Commander, you can still pull off some solid strategies with Ms. Bumbleflower that are really fun to play.

Food & Fellowship is one of the best Commander precons around right now, and it won't cost you an arm and a leg. It's led by Sam, Loyal Attendant, and Frodo, Adventurous Hobbit, and together they are the best Abzan Commander in the game right now, thanks to the Partner With mechanic.

Together, you'll create a ton of food tokens, all of which have their redemption cost reduced to just one colorless mana thanks to Sam, while Frodo works to tempt the Ring, letting you take free shots at other players and loot your deck with card draw and discarding.

There are so many fun and exciting ways to win with the Food & Fellowship Commander precon, and building a custom deck around Frodo and Sam is fun too, whether you stay within the Middle-earth theme or branch out into the Multiverse.

Kilo, Apogee Mind is about the most straightforward Commander on this list. A three-mana Jeskai Commander that enters as a 3/3 with Haste, Kilo is all about counters. Not the rejection kind, the +1/+1 and tracking kind. Whenever Kilo becomes tapped, you Proliferate. This means you may put an extra counter on any creature, enchantment, or artifact of the same kind that it already has (meaning you can't use Proliferate to put a counter on something that doesn't already have a counter).

Find ways to tap and untap Kilo at will, while dishing out +1/+1 counters to your creatures and other counters for your artifacts, and you'll soon find yourself winning games with ease. This is a hugely frustrating Commander to play against, but the best way to stop it is to play it yourself!

Backup Commander for the hugely popular Tarkir: Dragonstorm Commander precon, Sultai Arisen, Teval is a token-making machine that, similar to Kilo, can be hugely frustrating to play against.

Teval is a four-mana 4/4 with Flying, and whenever it attacks, you mill three cards. You may then return a land card from your graveyard to the battlefield tapped. Then, whenever one or more cards leave your graveyard, you create a 2/2 black Zombie Druid creature token.

The card synergies out there for Teval can move cards in and out of your battlefield at will, and create armies and armies of tokens that can easily withstand a few board wipes.

Edgar Markov is Mardu's best commander and still one of the best Commanders of all time. Eminence gives you an ability even if Edgar isn't on the battlefield, giving you a 1/1 Vampire for every Vampire cast. The Vampire doesn't even need to hit the battlefield to get the token.

You can build a deck around cheap Vampires (both monetarily and mana-wise) and still perform great because it's so easyto flood the battlefield. Edgar Markov is amazing because it does a ton without ever needing to cast it; its attacking ability is just a bonus.

The crown of best Temur Commander goes to Miirym, Sentinel Wyrm. It essentially doubles up on all your Dragon creatures when they enter the battlefield. Some cards can also double the number of tokens generated, giving you even more Dragon tokens.

Miirym only works with Dragons, but its built-in protection keeps it safe and harder to remove. The strongest Dragons are in Temur colors, letting you play the best ones, and if Miirym is on the battlefield, it even lets you get more than one copy.

We want to hear from you. Share your perspective in the comments below, and please keep the conversation respectful.

#4303. Marathon may actually have a shot as Server Slam hits it big on Steam

Marathon's latest public open weekend has kicked off, and it looks like enough people have showed up to play it.

Things are officially looking better for Marathon. The game’s Server Slam, essentially an open beta that’s freely available everywhere, has kicked off. This is the last chance for anyone curious about Bungie’s next big game to play it before it officially goes on sale next week.

Considering how unpopular the game has been throughout its development, and judging by the feedback from earlier closed beta tests, the turnout for the Server Slam is definitely encouraging.

The Marathon Server Slam has been online for a little over 12 hours on Steam, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S. Only one of those platforms shares player numbers, of course, but it's enough to offer some visibility into how popular the test has been.

Immediately after servers went live, Marathon shot up the Steam most played charts. The game quickly achieved a peak of 143,621 concurrent players (via SteamDB), which is very respectable. Given that the Server Slam will be available for the entire weekend, there’s every chance the numbers will go up.

These figures are particularly encouraging when you look at Arc Raiders, the current top dog in the extraction shooter space, and the game that stole Marathon’s thunder last year when the two of them were being promoted by their publishers. Marathon, of course, got delayed out of 2025, which allowed Arc Raiders to launch first. It, of course, ended up proving that extraction shooters can be mainstream hits.

Like Marathon, Arc Raiders hosted its own server slam just a few days before its launch. That open test attracted 189,668 concurrent players at its peak, which is not that far off from Marathon’s so far.

Assuming positive word of mouth continues, more players are bound to jump in over the weekend and perhaps get Marathon to match or even exceed Arc Raiders’ record. At any rate, this is good news for beleaguered Bungie and points to what could be a big launch.

Marathon arrives March 5 on PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S.

#4302. The Sims 4 is getting paid mods, and a new in-game currency to pay for them

The Sims 4 is about to launch a couple of major initiatives that may not exactly be what players have been looking for.

The Sims 4 has officially entered into its paid mods era. Developer Maxis announced The Sims Maker Program, and The Sims 4 Marketplace - two new destinations to publish, and discover new add-on content.

The two new features will arrive first on PC and Mac, starting March 17. PlayStation and Xbox players will receive them over the next couple of months, which is very much in line with how other franchises have rolled out their own paid mods systems.

The Maker Program is a way for community creators to get their work out there, and profit from it. The content they create will end up on the Marketplace, where other players can browse it, and pay for it if they want to use it in their game.

Created content will be available across all platforms. All previous packs The Sims 4 players should be familiar with will move to the Marketplace, too: once the feature launches, this is where you’re going to find Expansion Packs, Game Packs, Stuff Packs, Kits, and other official additions created by Maxis.

Alongside this, the game is also introducing a new virtual currency - Moola - which is what you’re going to use to purchase Maker Packs, as well as Sims 4 Kits in the Marketplace. A portion of your purchase will go to the creator (roughly 30%) of what you buy.

It is worth noting, however, that you’ll still be able to buy Expansion Packs, Game Packs, and Stuff Packs without having to purchase Moola, or go through the Marketplace. Kits are the only items that will no longer be available on the existing PC/console storefronts. Moola comes in the usual denominations you’ve seen a hundred items in other games’ in-game shops.

In order to start creating custom content and publishing it on the Marketplace, you’ll need to first be accepted into the program. Once that’s done, you’ll be able to directly publish your content on the Marketplace.

In the blog post announcing the new features, Maxis said that creators will have control over the price of their content, and how it's packaged. These are referred to as Maker Packs, which can include Create-a-Sim or Build/Buy items.

You can apply to become a Maker from March 5. Once accepted, you’ll also get access to the Maker Suite, which is what you’re going to use to test your work to ensure it runs smoothly on the different platforms, and eventually publish it.

#4301. Shigeru Miyamoto Proclaims November 1 is Pikmin Day, Pikmin 4 Demo Coming To Switch 2 Soon

This morning, Nintendo shared some updates related to the Pikmin franchise and has officially claimed November 1 as Pikmin Day, starting today and moving forward presumably forever.

Aside from the announcement of Pikmin Day as a general idea, Pikmin creator Shigeru Miyamoto appeared on camera to remind everyone that Pikmin 4 – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy is coming November 12. A free demo for the game, which will include one standard level and two Dandori Academy levels, will be available on November 2.

The Switch 2 version of the game (you can read Game Informer’s Pikmin 4 review here) will have improved visuals and take advantage of the Switch 2’s mic to let you say things like “Rush” and “Go to work” to Oatchi. The Dandori Academy side of the game is essentially time trials you can practice, and then on Fridays, Saturdays, and Sundays, you will have one chance to post your best time. You can read more about the Switch 2 version of the game here.

Miyamoto also shared that the mobile game, Pikmin Bloom, is also getting a fairly substantial update soon with secret caves. In Bloom, players will be able to find maps that reveal caves that you can send your Pikmin into to battle and find treasure. You can also find maps for Bloom by playing Pikmin 4. Caves will be coming to Pikmin Bloom later this year.

The Pikmin Day presentation also reminded viewers that every Pikmin game is available on Switch and Switch 2, though no announcements or hints were made implying that Pikmin 1 and 2 would be coming to the Nintendo Switch Online subscription service, which includes GameCube games on Switch 2. Those games can be purchased individually on the eShop.

Finally, Miyamoto brought actress Fuka Koshiba on the presentation (best known for voicing Kiki in Kiki’s Delivery Service) to share her appreciation for the Pikmin franchise (she likes to knit Pikmin hats that she shares on social media) and introduce a Pikmin short film. In the short, a Pikmin interacts with a toad, but I won’t spoil what happens. Miyamoto promised more shorts are on the way and in the future, they will be found in the Nintendo Today app.

Unfortunately, the stream concluded without a single reference to 2017's Hey! Pikmin. I wouldn't expect it to get a port to Switch 2 anytime soon.

#4300. 8 Remakes That Would Be Just As Meaningful As The Ocarina Of Time Remake

Aden Carter is a Contributor at DualShockers who has been covering games professionally since 2020. He specializes in lists and guides, with a focus on RPGs, horror games, survival horror, Soulslikes, cozy/sim games, and action-adventure titles. Before joining DualShockers, Aden contributed to GameRant, XDA, Gamepur, I

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake was one of the most anticipated remakes of all time. Year after year, fans would beg Nintendo to remake this masterpiece. In 2026, Nintendo finally listened, and the Ocarina of Time Remake was officially released.

The remake has received constant praise across the board, and fans are once again excited to jump into the land of Hyrule to stop Ganondorf and save the world.

This got me thinking. There have been many impactful games over the years, and while it is nice to see Ocarina of Time again, I bet there are other games that would be just as meaningful to fans if they were to be remade in the modern era.

Released back in 1999 on the PlayStation, Dino Crisis struck fear into the hearts of many, and it hit the same note as Resident Evil from years prior. Fans loved Capcom’s new style of horror game, and it has since become a cult classic, with a fan base that has been begging for the game to get a remake.

Dino Crisis took a step forward from the Resident Evil franchise, using real-time 3D environments. Along with this, the game featured slightly different mechanics that made it feel more tense.

While there have been some ports of the game, there has never been a remake. However, it is a game that is constantly mentioned whenever a discussion of remakes comes up, showing that fans are craving the original title.

There are quite a few Forgotten Capcom Games That Deserve A Remake in the modern day.

Whenever people talk about the Fallout franchise, they tend to gravitate towards either Fallout 3 or Fallout: New Vegas. All other Fallout titles are often ignored, and many even regard these two as being some of the best games ever made.

However, when it comes down to choosing between the two, people generally prefer Fallout: New Vegas. This is because of its superior roleplaying style and story. Meanwhile, the other is often considered to have a better atmosphere.

It has been said that a New Vegas remaster is in the works, and it will be around the same scope as the Oblivion remaster. However, if Bethesda were to completely remake the game, making it look better than even Fallout 4, then fans would go crazy for it. At least this is one game we know is coming back.

Star Wars has always been a huge franchise, and coming off the heels of the Star Wars: Episode II release was the hit titled Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic - a game that would become a fan favorite for generations.

This was one of BioWare’s best titles, and many remember it fondly to this day. It is a game that fans have begged to have remade. Unfortunately, a remake has never seen the light of day.

There have been rumors that got shut down, and even companies that have said they were working on it. Now, Saber Interactive is working on the Knights of the Old Republic Remake, but there has been little word about it for years. Fans never know if they will see this game in a new light, but when it finally gets released, it will rock the gaming industry.

Half-Life is considered one of the biggest masterpieces of gaming, and is also considered one of the most influential games for the shooter genre. It told the story of Gordon Freeman without ever needing to pull the camera away or break the mystique of the game.

The game pioneered seamless, scripted events, which made missions feel more cinematic. It also is known for having amazing environmental storytelling, with it using audio cues and NPC behaviours to communicate the story effectively.

There is a reason that Half-Life is known as one of the greatest games of all time. The franchise as a whole has been so impactful that fans are still begging for a third entry in the series.

Today, many are focused on the release of Grand Theft Auto VI, and for good reason. Many are saying it will be Rockstar’s greatest game. However, a remake of a past title of theirs would be a bit more meaningful.

If the team decided to remake Grand Theft Auto III, it would hit hard for many who lived through the era of the early 2000s. After all, GTA III is said to be the pioneer of the modern open world, with it giving players access to a fully open 3D environment known as Liberty City.

This game went on to influence many others, such as Saints Row and Mafia. Without it, we might not have open world games as we know them, and if it were to be remade in a modern engine, fans would lose their minds.

There is no denying that Ocarina of Time is the most influential of all the Zelda titles released over the years. Also released around the time of the original Ocarina of Time was a narrative sequel that fans remember just as much to this day.

Of course, I am referring to The Legend of Zelda: Majora’s Mask. This is another masterpiece of a Zelda title that has stood the test of time and is still talked about to this day.

While Ocarina of Time made fans hopeful, Majora’s Mask took the story down a dark path, and it is one that heavily impacted those who played it back in the day. If there is another Zelda title that deserves the same remake treatment, it is this one.

Eiji Aonuma and the development team for the Ocarina of Time remake discussed how one of the original's infamous dungeons is being improved.

If you owned an N64 back in the day, odds are you played Super Mario 64. This is yet another classic N64 title that fans love and has been played to death. If any other game matches up to the popularity of Ocarina of Time, it would be Super Mario 64.

This game pioneered special movement in a 3D environment, allowing players to freely explore the Mushroom Kingdom with a fully functional camera. It is one of the most impactful games that has ever been released.

For many, this is the first time they saw Mario enter the 3D realm, and it is a game that has stuck with gamers for generations. There are even those who speedrun the game on a yearly basis.

Chrono Trigger is one of Square Enix’s most celebrated titles. Released back in 1995 on the SNES, the game told a story that spanned multiple eras of time, as heroes tried to prevent the world from ending.

Over the years, Chrono Trigger has received multiple ports, with it appearing on mobile devices, the Nintendo DS, and also the PlayStation. These ports have received praise from the community, with the DS port receiving a 92 from review scores.

Many have asked for this masterpiece to be reimagined in HD-2D over the years, and some have even asked for it to receive the Final Fantasy VII Remake treatment. Unfortunately, there has never been an official announcement of a remake, but it would instantly become a major hit if it was.

While some JRPGs disappear, others return from oblivion after years without new releases.

#4299. Our first look at Diablo 4's Warlock and the game's next season arrive in today's livestream - watch it here

Diablo 4's latest Developer Update is nearly upon us, and it's one plenty of the game's fans and players have been looking forward to.

Diablo 4’s next, long-awaited Developer Update finally airs today. This meaty livestream was first announced nearly a month ago, when Blizzard initially revealed that the game’s next class is the Warlock.

The Warlock’s initial unveiling, however, was incredibly brief, showing no gameplay. It also didn't explain how the class is going to fit within the existing roster. This all changes today.

Blizzard is bringing back its Developer Update livestream programme, which is the more structured, information-dense series of developer showcases. The focus of this one, of course, is going to mainly be on the Warlock class.

The Warlock is one of two classes coming to Diablo 4 with the upcoming Lord of Hatred expansion. The first, the Paladin, is already available in the game for anyone who pre-orders the expansion. The Warlock will instead arrive alongside the expansion on April 28.

The Developer Update will also include a first look at the game’s next season (Season 12), currently set for March 10. This mini season will only last until the expansion’s release, so it’s going to be interesting to see what it brings to the game.

You’ll be able to watch the showcase live at 11am PT, 2pm ET, 7pm GMT on Diablo 4’s official YouTube, Twitch, and Twitter channels. We’ve embedded the YouTube and Twitch players below for your convenience.

Among the topics the Developer Update will cover are the Killstreaks system, as well as Bloodstained items. As always, you can also expect a Q&A segment at the end of the show, and I imagine there’s going to be a few about the Warlock.

#4297. Pokemon Music Box Dioramas For All Regions Are Being Sold In Japan

The Pokemon Center has started selling music box dioramas and framed maps for all nine of the franchise’s regions, but you’re going to have a tough time getting your hands on them.

For as long as Pokemon has been around, it’s had some of the best merchandise in gaming. Not even counting the unbelievable amount of gorgeous and sought-after cards for the TCG, there are skateboard decks, Lego sets, plushes, golden figures, playsets, and oh so much more. Just look at the branded cans of soup, if you somehow need more proof.

Since there's clearly no shortage of Pokemon goods in the world already, you’d think that there’s not much left that could possibly leave an impression. Well, you might want to change that tune, as the Pokemon Center has just revealed an incredible new collection of dioramas and framed maps that are going to leave you cursing if you’re not in Japan.

As pointed out by Dexerto, the official Japanese Pokemon site recently shared a blog post detailing a new collection that’s being added to the online store on November 12. The collection focuses on the “evolution of the Pokemon series” and includes music box dioramas representing locations from each region in the series, framed maps, and paper crafts.

Watching thousands of Pokemon Go players gather in Chicago showed me that the game's greatest feature has always been community.

Pokemon is no stranger to dioramas, but these music boxes are absolutely gorgeous, featuring nicely crafted replicas of areas like Route 1 alongside acrylic or 3D figures of the respective generation’s starter Pokemon and, of course, Pikachu. It’s really just the cherry on top that they also serve as a music box.

My favourite of the bunch has to be Route 3 from Sword and Shield, which has a lovely figure of my fave Scorbunny.

Those dioramas are selling for 12,100 yen, which equates to around $76, so they’re not exactly cheap, but they are very cool. The framed maps are equally gorgeous and going for around $105, while the paper crafts are just over $24. Of course, there’s a big catch to all of this, as the items are all exclusive to the Japanese Pokemon Center Online store.

Like with all Pokemon Center Online merchandise, there’s a chance that we see it come to other parts of the world later down the line. Until then, though, you’re either going to have to figure out a workaround or dare to look into the depths of reselling and scalpers. That’s just another day ending in Y for Pokemon fans, though.

Pokemon has entertained both children and adults alike for several generations. Whether hit video games, anime series and movies, trading cards, or more, there's something for every budding trainer hoping to catch 'em all.

We opened 49 packs of the new set, this is what we thought.

#4296. Diablo 4's next season is short, but it lets you become The Butcher, and it has Doom: The Dark Ages skins you probably can't afford

Blizzard has unveiled the next Diablo 4 season, which kicks off next week to hold us over until the launch of the game's big expansion in April.

The big Diablo 4 Developer Update has indeed delivered the goods. One of the livestream’s big topics was, of course, the game’s upcoming mini-season, which is set to kick off next week and run until the launch of Lord of Hatred, the game’s anticipated next expansion.

You can tell Blizzard wanted to have a bit of fun with Season of Slaughter, as many of its major features make it look like a limited-time event, but there is plenty to be excited about here.

Season of Slaughter kicks off March 11, and will run until the following season kicks off April 28, with the launch of the Lord of Hatred expansion. Many of the season’s biggest additions were available to preview in the 2.6.0 Public Test Realm.

Patch 2.6.0, as you might have guessed, is the one that will kick off the slaughter next week. The headline feature here is ability to become The Butcher, the iconic in-game boss who randomly invades players’ games.

When you play as The Butcher, you’ll be rewarded the more kills you get in quick succession. Your skills hotbar will transform to become something more fitting of The Butcher, making them more brutal. You’ll also earn a seasonal currency as you play.

Starting the seasonal questline is how you can begin to assume The Butcher’s form. A Taste of Power can be initiated from Gea Kul. Transforming into The Butcher can be done in a few ways. As you play, you’ll earn Meaty Offerings, which can later be spent on Shrines of Slaughter in the new Helltide. Once activated, the shrine will draw more enemies towards you.

If you never venture into PvP zones in Diablo 4, this season may change your mind. The standard PvP combat that could only be found in Fields of Hatred has been replaced with a Ceremony of Slaughter, a new event that rewards you for killing enemies quickly. See it through and The Butcher’s Idol will spawn, allowing you to transform into it.

Elsewhere in the world, you’ll also be able to attain the same power at Slaughterhouses, a new activity type available this season. Inside, you immediately become The Butcher for the entirety of the run.

The Butcher’s arrival also ties into two of the other Season of Slaughter’s more interesting additions. First, the Killstreak system finally arrives in Diablo 4, rewarding you for being as efficient as possible in carving your way through enemies.

Anyone who played Diablo 3 should be familiar with how it works. It kicks off the moment you get a kill, and has a visible timer where you’ll need continue performing the same action to up your streak. The more kills you get, the more often your timer will refresh.

There are five tiers to climb through: Killstreak, Carnage, Devastation, Bloodbath, and Massacre. You’re awarded for the tier you manage to reach before the timer runs out. You’ll earn XP and seasonal rep each time a Killstreak is achieved.

The other Butcher-themed addition is Bloodied Items, which is a new item quality available throughout this season. They play into the Killstreak system to grant you even more power. Bloodied Items come with unique affixes that scale off your Killstreak tier. You’ll see many familiar items in that pool, as any item in the game has a chance to drop as Bloodied. Bloodied Items can also be acquired by earning Fresh Meat.

Even if none of that sounds exciting, you’re probably going to redownload the game for The Paladin free trial, which kicks off alongside the new season on March 11. The trial is only available until March 18, and it lets you try out the Paladin class.

The trial is available across PC, PlayStation, and Xbox. You’ll be able to take the new class for a spin, but your progress will be capped at level 25. The Paladin can be permanently unlocked by buying the Lord of Hatred expansion, as it’s one of two classes the expansion is introducing.

The good news is that any progress you make in the free trial will carry over to the full game if/when you buy the expansion.

Season of Slaughter also kicks off a Doom: The Dark Ages collaboration event. As we’ve come to expect, there’s a very limited free component to the collaboration, in the form of the Doom Reliquary. This is essentially a mini-battle pass that includes the Shield Saw skin, Slayer’s Flair, the head of the Cyberdemon as a back trophy and various other smaller bits.

The more impressive items - such as character skins, will instead be available to purchase for real money. The list includes the Doom Slayer armor, Mecha Dragon Serrat skin for your cat mount, and a Cacodemon pet.

Though the armor skin is cross-class compatible, judging by how much previous collaboration items have cost in Diablo 4, most of us probably won’t be spending that kind of money to get it.

#4295. Yakuza Creator Toshiro Nagoshi's Studio Has Officially Shut Down, Ending Gang Of Dragon's Development With It

Nagoshi Studio, the developer led by Yakuza/Like a Dragon series creator Toshiro Nagoshi, has officially shut down, ending development of Gang of Dragon, which was revealed at The Game Awards last year. Shareholders resolved to dissolve the studio on October 31, according to a notice published in a Japanese government newspaper called Kanpo, as first reported by Gematsu.

This follows a report from Bloomberg earlier this year that said Chinese gaming megacorp NetEase Games was cutting funding to Nagoshi Studio, allowing Nagoshi to seek independent funding elsewhere. It seems he couldn't find funding, and now Nagoshi Studio is no more. NetEase helped Nagoshi found the studio in November 2021.

You can watch the Gang of Dragon reveal trailer below for a look at what the team was cooking up:

This closure follows other signals that NetEase is looking to divest from the gaming scene outside of its Chinese studios. A little over a month ago, Suda51's Grasshopper Manufacture left NetEase to go independent again, just months after the launch of Romeo Is A Dead Man.

#4294. PHYSINT Star Bill Skarsgård has Become ‘Enamored’ with Hideo Kojima and His Works

Daniel is a lifelong gamer with a love for various genres and gameplay styles who enjoys exploring games and playing from various angles.

If a single person could be considered to be the definitive face of auteur game development, it would be Hideo Kojima, hands down. The man was already showing his chops in putting together unforgettable productions back in the Metal Gear Solid days, and ever since going into business for himself with Kojima Productions, his worlds and stories have only gotten bigger and bolder.

All of those qualities alone more than qualify Kojima for auteur status, but there’s also a little bit more to it than that. Kojima possesses, for lack of a better term, a certain magnetism, both in his person and his production, that inexplicably draws powerful, prominent individuals from across the entertainment spectrum. You just have to look at the original Death Stranding and its star-studded cast to see the kind of magnetic pull a Kojima trip possesses.

Very little is currently known about PHYSINT, one of Kojima’s next big-budget productions that was rescued from the brink by XBOX when Sony bailed out over the summer, but apparently, its star, Bill Skarsgård, was already well aboard Mister Kojima’s wild ride well before he signed on. He spoke to this during a recent appearance on the Happy Sad Confused podcast, as well as the inherent power that comes with Kojima’s works.

Joining an already stacked cast for PHYSINT, which features Charlee Fraser, Don Lee, and Minami Hamabe, is none other than Bill Skarsgård.

As Skarsgård explained, he grew up playing Kojima’s games during his time at Konami, chief among them the Metal Gear series. By his own admission, Skarsgård has played every single Metal Gear game that is commercially available, finding himself repeatedly drawn into the elaborate, intricate world that Kojima was piecing together story-by-story.

Skarsgård has played every single Metal Gear game that is commercially available.

As Skarsgård became more interested in Kojima’s creations, he became more interested in Kojima himself. “I was very enamoured by him and the sort of the mythology or the universes that he creates, but also the sort of mystique and allure about him as well,” he explained.

Hideo Kojima shared several new details about PHYSINT, and it looks like the legendary developer is going back to full stealth.

Later in the interview, as Skarsgård described the process of motion capture that was going into PHYSINT’s development, he marveled at how the planned game will feature both eight hours of narrative alongside an entire, living world populated by photorealistic people and settings.

“I think he's a pioneer, and keeps going out to untrodden waters,” he said of Kojima.

Skarsgård briefly recalled a discussion he had about filmmaking with Kojima during PHYSINT’s motion capture process. It’s no secret that, in addition to video games, Kojima is well-versed in the cinematic arts, both on a technical level and just as a good old fashioned lover of movies, as you can tell from the many film references and direct shout-outs that pepper his games.

Interestingly, though, when Skarsgård asked Kojima if he ever wanted to make an actual movie someday rather than a game, Kojima said no, because he wants to make something with the cinematic potential of traditional film combined with the inherent interactivity of a video game, and a regular film can’t do that. “At this point, what he's doing is inventing a new medium,” Skarsgård said.

All we currently know about PHYSINT, aside from its major stars in Bill Skarsgård, Charlee Fraser, Ma Dong-seok, and Minami Hamabe, is that it’s apparently going to be an action-espionage game in a similar vein to the Metal Gear series. The promotional tagline on its initial reveal poster is “The Next Cold War Begins.” Based on Skarsgård’s gushing, though, it’s going to be quite the ambitious multimedia project, the kind of elaborate, once-per-generation creation that only an auteur like Kojima could bring to life. So, y’know, business as usual.

New PHYSINT exhibition displays feature Metal Gear-like mechs, offering an intriguing glimpse of Kojima's next spy-action game.

#4293. Diablo 4’s Warlock looks like an unhinged Necromancer with Sorcerer energy in first look at gameplay

Diablo 4's practitioner of forbidden arts, The Warlock, has been officially unveiled as the second class coming with Lord of Hatred.

Thanks to a meaty, well-produced Diablo 4 Developer Update, we got to have our promised first look at gameplay of the Warlock, the second of two classes coming to the game with the upcoming Lord of Hatred expansion.

The showcase offered a deep look at the Warlock’s core archetypes, its gameplay and skills loop, and where the class sits within the game’s existing roster of diverse classes.

Since the initial reveal of Lord of Hatred, The Warlock has remained the mysterious second class. Anyone who pre-purchased the expansion was able to get immediate access to The Paladin, the other class arriving with the expansion. It wasn’t until February that Blizzard officially revealed the class to the world, but we had to wait until this most recent Developer Update to actually see it in action.

The Warlock’s pragmatism exists as the counterpart to The Paladin's purity, in that Warlocks don’t shy away from harnessing the powers of Hell to eliminate their enemies. The class can conjure up demons to do their bidding, and utilise attacks previously only available to legions of Hell.

The Warlock is a hybrid pet and caster class. Their gameplay revolves around summoning demons, and undermining enemies with shadow arts. They rely on two resources: Wrath, and Dominance. Casting Skills consumes Wrath, whereas Dominance is what allows the Warlock to summon and exploit demons.

The Warlock has four archetypes players can spec into. Legions are traditional summoners who rely on overwhelming numbers to crush enemies. Vanguards are closer to Sorcerers, capable of dealing damage head-on. Masterminds utilise shadowcraft to slowly drain their enemies. Finally, Ritualists are summoners of the most terrifying Hell demons.

The Warlock is able to do this by fusing Soul Shards into their bodies. Going down any of the four paths becomes available after reaching level 30, which is when the class mechanic is unlocked. Each Soul Shard is tied to a certain demon, and its through that power that the Warlock is able to call upon them in combat. Your choice does, of course, affect your abilities going forward.

Warlocks arrive alongside new Uniques that cater to their specific playstyles, which is similar to what we’ve previously seen with The Paladin, and The Spiritborn before that.

Lord of Hatred arrives April 28. While we wait, Diablo 4’s next season is kicking off next week to deliver a bit of mindless fun to hold us over until the big day.

#4291. GTA 6 Could Get PC Release Soon to Avoid AI Clones, Says Former Rockstar Dev

Lauren has experience in the gaming and esports space, writing news, guides, features, reviews, lists, conducting interviews, and more. Before joining the team at DualShockers, Lauren was a Features Writer at Adventure Gamers, a Guides Writer at Gameranx, as well as contributing as a News Writer at PCInvasion and Daily

The launch of GTA 6 is imminent, and thanks to Rockstar Games moving the pre-load date forward, the release of this highly anticipated game is starting to feel more real. However, not even the big dogs are safe from the likes of AI, as there are concerns Generative AI could be used by third parties to port the game on PC.

It’s becoming increasingly common to see an indie hit take off and AI-generated clones quickly following in an attempt to piggy back off of that success. One such example is the viral Needle In A Haystack game, which follows the premise of finding a needle hidden in over 10 million pieces of hay with your friends. Since then, various AI-generated rip offs began appearing on Steam, with one developer even stealing the original game’s code.

Rockstar's 38 new GTA 6 screenshots showcase incredibly detailed faces, Vice City's nightlife, and the gangs and scenes bringing Leonida to life.

Roblox is another platform that Needle In A Haystack, among other trending games, has popped up on. Since Roblox is free to play, anyone can play a near copy of a paid game, with a few microtransactions thrown in.

Although GTA 6 would be difficult to replicate in the same way, former Rockstar North technical director, Obbe Vermeij, believes AI is a threat to an official GTA 6 PC port, as discussed in an interview with Rock Paper Shotgun.

Vermeij acknowledges that Generative AI “really has changed the world," and believes, “I would be concerned, if I was Rockstar, that somebody would just take the PS5 version and get AI to change it to PC, which won't be as good as their effort, but it could still also hurt their sales. So, I wouldn't be surprised if there was an effort to get [the releases] a little bit closer together. Obviously, I don't really know what they're thinking."

"I don't really see how you could protect against that, to be honest, I don't see it," he says, but Take-Two Interactive aren’t completely powerless on the matter. “But a big company like Take-Two, they would be able to get the lawyers on the case, and maybe, like, you said, for a big game, maybe the AI doesn't really do a particularly good job.”

“But yeah, I mean, it's a brave new world. What was the case before, is that there's so much effort in developing the game, that it is not possible to rip it off, and that's completely changed now. So, yeah, we're going to have to see in the next couple of years, how that's going to pan out."

It has been widely reported that GTA 6 will be released on PC during the first quarter of 2027. Neither Rockstar Games nor Take-Two has provided comment on the status of the arrival of GTA 6 on PC.

Not even the big dogs are safe from the likes of AI, as there are concerns Generative AI could be used by third parties to port the game on PC.

If GTA 6 does make its PC debut in the first quarter of 2027, it would land just a few months after its release on PlayStation 5 and XBOX Series X|S platforms. Therefore, it would be a lot quicker than the PC release of GTA 5, which came out in April 2015, nearly two years after its roll out on console in September 2013.

Any AI-generated ports would likely face a DMCA takedown and will undoubtedly be nowhere near as polished or safe to run than the real deal.

As AI continues to advance, it will be interesting to see if it’s able to replicate a game as huge as GTA 6. The game is expected to require up to 212 GB of storage on console and is packed to the brim with approximately 80 hours of story content alone.

From DMA Design to GTA III, GTA V, and RDR2, let's take a look back at how Rockstar Games changed open-world gaming and why GTA 6 has so much to live up to.

#4290. Ocarina Of Time Newcomers Are Getting Killed By Cuccos

The driving force behind Nintendo wanting to remake The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is to give new fans, some who weren’t even born when the original was released, a modernized version of the game that they’re more likely to fall in love with. As some of those new fans have quickly discovered, that also means learning tougher lessons older fans had to learn 28 years ago.

As much as the way we play games may have changed since the launch of the original Ocarina, there are some things that remain the same. One of those things is that you put a gamer into a virtual space with some hapless chickens, or cuccos since this is Zelda, those chickens are going to get messed with.

We finally got a chance to play The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake and it's still one of the best games ever made.

Cuccos are a staple of the Zelda series, and you encounter them frequently in Ocarina of Time. Veterans know not to attack them, learning the hard way 28 years ago that doing so means they’ll attack you right back. Turns out that detail has been retained for the remake, and streamer IShowSpeed found out about the legendary detail the hard way.

Less than two hours into a livestream of his Ocarina remake playthrough, Speed’s chat coaxed him into attacking a cucco. Upon being struck with Link’s sword, the cucco crows and summons all of its friends, which rain down from the sky, chipping away at your health, just like they did in Ocarina on the N64.

There is no escape, so all Speed can do is panic and run around until his health has been depleted. Turns out that was the first time he died. I know that because he started screaming it at the chat who tricked him into hurting a cucco after the screen faded to black.

Don’t worry, Speed, you’re not the only new Zelda fan playing Ocarina for the first time this week who thought they could attack a cucco without paying for it dearly. Streamer Hika has also shared a clip where she dared to swing her sword at a cucco in Hyrule Castle Town, only to then feel the wrath of all of the avian victim’s feathered friends. “I must be the only one who didn’t know this was happening?” Hika’s tweet reads. No, Hika, turns out you’re not alone.

There are so many people already playing the Ocarina remake that details regarding what has changed and what has remained faithful to the original have quickly been discovered. Cucco attacks have crossed the remake barrier. However, some of the references to other games, including Mario, have been removed as Nintendo didn’t want to disrupt the remake’s immersion.

#4289. Marathon launch player numbers are about half those of the Server Slam, at least on PC

Marathon hasn't quite been able to attract the same volume of players the recent Server Slam did.

After a couple of delays, a plagiarism lawsuit, and at least one internal reboot, Bungie’s next big game has officially launched. Marathon, the extraction shooter from the studio behind Destiny, has managed to find a decent, if a little small of an audience.

The game’s player numbers on Steam are being compared to its recent free, open weekend, and not in a favourable manner.

Prior to Marathon’s launch, Bungie held a multi-day Server Slam, which offered anyone interested in playing the game a chance to try out almost all of its classes, two of its maps, as well as many of its gameplay and progression systems.

The open test was largely well-received, and players actually showed up for it. It peaked at a very respectable 143,621 concurrent players on Steam, which put it within striking distance of the peak concurrent of its chief competitor, Arc Raiders - at least when you compare both of their pre-launch Server Slam events.

In Arc Raiders’ case, those figures were far outpaced at the game’s actual launch, and the Embark shooter continues to command a very active player base to this day. A paid product garnering far more players than the same product’s own free sampler is never not a good sign, so many hoped something similar would happen with Marathon.

Marathon has now officially launched, and it doesn’t look like it managed to pull an Arc Raiders - at least so far. At its peak, the Bungie shooter attracted 88,337 concurrent players on Steam (via SteamDB), which is a little over half of its Server Slam’s 143,621 peak concurrent.

Numbers have, of course, dropped since then, which is normal, as players log off for the night. This is obviously not the end of the road for Marathon. Friday, and the weekend, may well push numbers closer to the Server Slam heights.

Indeed, word of mouth is quite positive, with the game currently sitting at a Very Positive user review rating on Steam, based on over 4,600 reviews. As has been proven time and time again in recent years, nothing catapults a game like players emphatically advocating for it to their friends, so it could simply be that mainstream players are cautious.

It will become clear where things settle over the weekend.

#4288. The Elder Scrolls VI Has An Official Subtitle And It's 'Sentinel'

The headline tells the story: The Elder Scrolls VI has an official subtitle and it's Sentinel. So the full game is now titled The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel, or, as we will undoubtedly refer to it moving forward, as we colloquially do with the previous three games (Morrowind, Oblivion, and Skyrim), Sentinel.

The news comes from Bethesda's various social media accounts, which are all sharing the video above. Along with the video, music, and the title, it also shares the text as a quote attributed to Yazar, Moth Priest to High Queen Iradne of Hammerfell (4E 206): "The scroll offered only a shimmer, a veil thinly lifted to my eyes. A future lost. A victory undone. Sands of time scattered by fate."

Sentinel is one of the nine major kingdoms within Hammerfell and is the capital of both the Alik'r Desert region and the Myrkwasa region of the Alik'r (source: elderscrolls.fandom). With this knowledge, it's fair to assume Sentinel will have many desert locations.

The name continues the tradition of naming the games after locations in the Elder Scrolls universe. Oblivion is the sort of exception, as it is a realm, but it still counts. We still don't know exactly when The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel will be released, but we're now about seven years from its original announcement at E3 2018.

#4287. Nintendo Switch Sports Resort Review: Everything Switch Sports Should Have Been

Wuhu Island is back, and so is the magic. Nintendo Switch Sports Resort finally recaptures the charm that made me fall for this series years ago.

Say Nintendo Switch Sports Resort three times in a row. Go on, I’ll wait. It’s a tongue twister of a title, and I tripped over it every single time, which is at complete odds with the smoothness the game delivered.

The Nintendo DS didn’t just have great games, it had ideas that stuck around way longer than anyone expected.

I have played every entry in this series. When the Wii turned waving a remote around the living room into a whole new way of playing, I was right there, and I’ve had a soft spot for motion controls ever since. I do enjoy a good sports game, but if I’m honest, it’s mostly Nintendo’s that get me off the sofa. That’s also why I always worry a little whenever a new one is announced, because Nintendo Switch Sports never quite managed to feel like the series I fell in love with.

DualShockers was given a code for this review, and I’ve spent multiple hours on Wuhu Island so far, mostly in single player, on a docked Switch 2. I am nowhere near 100%, and I suspect that could take hundreds of hours depending on how good you are. But the hours I have put in have been more than enough to know this is the game I wanted Switch Sports to be.

The first thing I noticed was how little I was waiting. Load times are much shorter than in Nintendo Switch Sports, menus snap into place, and you can even rearrange the layout of the sports to suit you. Everything feels smoother, less clunky and quicker to get going. After the last entry, that alone felt like a small miracle.

Nintendo games always feel good, and I went in with high expectations of polish. Nintendo Switch Sports Resort met every single one of them. It ran perfectly on my docked Switch 2, and I didn’t run into a single bug or crash in my time playing this. Why can’t every game feel this polished?

My first birdie in Golf and my first strike in Bowling both made me grin like an idiot. It turns out the muscle memory I built up over years of these games is fully transferable, and it all just feels a bit more refined now. Bowling and Golf are still my favourites, Table Tennis gives you lovely control over every return, and Archery is so satisfying that I kept going back for “just one more” target. Tennis now comes with three courts to choose from, which is nice, if hardly a revolution.

Not everything landed quite as well. Boxing was the one I enjoyed least, because the Joy-Con 2 occasionally lost track of me once I mixed in ducks, hooks and jabs. Volleyball, unfortunately, still feels very sluggish, and that carries over into online play, too. It’s my single biggest deduction, and it’s a shame, because Volleyball also gave me one of my favourite moments.

Picture this: deuce after deuce, a match that seemingly will not end, my arms burning. By the time it was over, I was panting and had to sit down and rethink a few of my life choices. Nintendo, if you’re reading this, I desperately need a new Ring Fit Adventure, because that game actually kept me fit.

Then there’s Thumb Wrestling. It’s such an odd addition, and it makes me laugh every time, because it is so very Nintendo. It’s simple to pick up, there’s more strategy to it than you’d ever expect, and I can already see it causing chaos at parties. And yet.

I cannot believe they included Thumb Wrestling over my beloved Baseball. I’d have taken Disc Golf from the original Wii Sports Resort, too. Some of the racket and net sports also start to blur together after a while, so a little more variety would have gone a long way.

My favourite part of Resort is the trio of Leisure Sports, which have nothing to do with winning and everything to do with simply enjoying the island. Power Cruising puts you on a jet ski, with a Joy-Con held sideways like handlebars, twisting to accelerate and leaning to steer. Prop Plane turns your controller into a little aeroplane in your hand, and Skateboarding uses mouse mode, so you swipe across the table to push off and flick upwards for tricks. Luckily, the Nintendo Switch 2’s Welcome Tour trained me for exactly that moment. Generally, these sports are the most creative controls in the whole game, and they’re where I spent a lot of my down time.

Each of them comes with a Sightseeing Tour, where you have five minutes to explore and collect as much as you can. I’ll admit the timer sometimes had me wishing for more. There is a Free Roam mode without one, but none of the collectibles appear there, so it’s more of a scenic drive than a treasure hunt.

There’s no story in Resort, not really, but the sightseeing is the closest it gets. Finding photo spots and cruising past corners of Wuhu Island I’d never seen before taught me more about the place than any previous entry. It’s also the perfect palate cleanser after a sweaty round of Volleyball.

Hyrule has never looked better as they look in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake, and critics seem to agree!

Very quickly I discovered probably the number one reason that will keep me playing for months: everything counts now. In Nintendo Switch Sports, you could only earn the points needed to unlock new outfits and accessories by playing online. In Switch Sports Resort, every game you finish earns you points, single player included, and you spend them in a shop that rotates its collections weekly and monthly. You don’t even need a Nintendo Switch Online Membership anymore!

What you can pull from the shop is random and different for every user. It covers clothes, accessories, name tag options and sporting gear. On top of that, each sport has its own achievements, which you can unlock solo or with friends. As a bit of an achievement collector, that’s dangerous news for my free time.

For anyone who wants more of a challenge, Island Crown sets you up against increasingly skilled CPU players in each sport, with an Island Champ waiting at the top. The first few opponents are almost charmingly bad, but the tougher ones are genuinely tough. Nintendo has also added a little more “canon” this time, with each sport’s champion getting a bit of backstory. I haven’t beaten a single Champ yet, but I’m working on it.

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort looks gorgeous. It’s bursting with colour and that typical Nintendo charm, and I never once got tired of looking at it. The soundtrack is upbeat and light-hearted, and returning players will recognise plenty of the sound cues. My favourite detail? In Golf, you can hear the waves crashing against the shore and birds chirping between your shots.

The island itself never feels empty. Miis stroll around in the background, and even the CPU opponents use the little stickers that are the game’s only way of communicating. You can play as the newer-style characters and the classic Miis, which made me happier than I’d like to admit. Every session left me feeling a little brighter, which is exactly what I want from this series.

Accessibility has taken a step forward, too. You can choose your dominant hand for every sport, turn on a colourblind mode, and switch off the emote pop-ups from other players and CPUs if you find them distracting. Golf has assistance options, and the tutorials are clear and helpful. You are still tied to the Joy-Cons and motion controls, though: there are no alternative control schemes, and nothing can be remapped.

This is a game for literally everyone. If you just want some fun, need something to play with your family or friends, or want an excuse to move a bit more, this game has you covered. You can play with one to four people locally, go online, take on CPU opponents, and even team up with a CPU partner in some sports. I can already see it becoming the focal point of many a games night.

What surprised me most is how good it is on your own. It’s the most fun I’ve had in a while, even playing completely alone. Games like this usually lose steam once the novelty wears off, but there’s so much variety here that I’m nowhere near running out of things to do.

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort looks gorgeous. It’s bursting with colour and that typical Nintendo charm, and I never once got tired of looking at it.

Online play does have a couple of bumps in typical Nintendo fashion. Bowling has some strange waits between turns, and switching sports kicks you back to the lobby. These are pretty small complaints, though, when everything around them is this good. If anything, Nintendo has undersold this one: for how much better it is than its predecessor, it deserved a much bigger marketing push.

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort is a great revival for a series I’m always a little worried about. Nintendo is one of the only AAA players left that still brings real whimsy to the table, and Resort feels fresh, special, and complete from day one. If you want a sports game with actual substance, rather than a handful of minigames, this is the one. If you’d rather sink into a big story, look elsewhere – and if you hate fun? Honestly, I’m not sure how you ended up reading a review about Wii Sports' cheerful grandchild, but I admire the commitment. Somewhere on Wuhu Island, an Island Champ is waiting for me. I might not be ready yet. But I want to become the Island Legend, so I will keep training.

#4286. Nintendo's Inventory Levels At A Record High As RAM Crisis Continues

As part of its latest financial report, Nintendo has published the yen value of its inventory for the second quarter of FY2026/27, showing a record high as the company attempts to mitigate rising costs across the industry.

The latest quarterly report states that the platform holder has 814.57 billion yen's worth (approximately £3.8 billion / $5.14 billion) of inventory in its warehouses as of 30th September. That's an increase from 539.8 billion yen the previous quarter.

As highlighted by Nintendo Patents Watch, this is a new record for the firm as manufacturers across tech sectors navigate the global RAM shortage and attempt to avoid — or at least delay — further price increases.

Another quarter, another new record of inventory level. In just three months, Nintendo increased the inventories by ¥197B to a total of ¥815B (~US$5.15B). This is an astronomical number for a video game company, but is necessary to hedge against rising memory costs.

Nintendo raised the cost of Switch 2 worldwide earlier this year, following in the footsteps of Sony and Microsoft, who have hiked hardware prices multiple times in recent years.

It's a tough time for the industry, with recent reports suggesting that Microsoft's next Xbox could cost as much as $1800. The massive costs of developing and manufacturing systems and sourcing the necessary memory and components arguably put Nintendo in a better position than the competition in the short term, as both PS5 and Xbox Series X|S launched in 2020 compared to 2025 for Switch 2.

Nintendo managed to build a substantial inventory of Switch 2 units prior to launch and will want to have as many units as possible available ahead of the holidays following today's launch of Zelda: Ocarina of Time and the recent Zelda 40th Anniversary Switch 2.

It is worth noting that Nintendo's research and development costs rose 16.8% to 96.2 billion yen this quarter. This lends credence to rumours that the firm may be developing a 'Switch 2 Lite' or other hardware, although we wouldn't expect to see any revised hardware announcements anytime soon.

For comparison, Switch Lite arrived in 2019, two-and-a-half years after the launch of Switch 1. Assuming a similar timescale, Holiday 2027 could be the target launch window for a hypothetical Switch 2 Lite, but given the industry climate and challenges — not to mention the wider economy — that feels ambitious.

#4285. Nioh 3 patch finally makes summons useful in boss fights, brings free armour for everyone

There's a new Nioh 3 patch out in the wild, and it's one that any player who regularly summons in boss fights will really appreciate.

Team Ninja continues to work on Nioh 3. The developer has been releasing regular updates for the action RPG since its launch in early February. Earlier patches have addressed major bugs like healing item use inconsistencies, and more have arrived since to tackle various balance and loot-related issues.

Today’s patch, version 1.04, is a major one, coming in at well over 1GB. There’s plenty here worth getting excited about, so let’s dig in.

To begin with, this is the patch that adds the promised free armour sets for both Ninja, and Samurai. When Nioh 3 reached one million sales, Team Ninja said it would gift every player the Thunderous set in celebration, and the set’s two variants are now available in-game.

The more interesting side of the patch is, unsurprisingly, its change log. There appears to be a focus on online co-op and AI summons in this one, with various tweaks to the make the process more rewarding, and, in some cases, worthwhile.

The amount of Glory obtained when you complete a mission in multiplayer has been increased, regardless of which player was the host. The other major change mainly affects AI Benevolent Grave summons, making it so bosses will no longer target a single player for almost the entirety of the fight.

While summoning AI helpers has always been useful in Nioh 3, they didn’t always help in boss fights, specifically because the boss tended to focus on the player who summoned them, leaving the AI to run around eating AoE hits before dying.

Patch 1.04 makes a couple of welcome gameplay tweaks to the feel of combat. Ninjutsu, and Onmyo Magic will now hit their targets more consistently in situations where there’s a difference in elevation between the player and the enemy.

In the same vein, you’ll now be able to attack (quick/strong) right after jumping, which removes the pause that previously buffered the attack instead. This could mean even more air combos that don’t specifically require Martial Arts.

You can look forward to a couple of quality of life tweaks in this patch, too, such as the change that allows the game to automatically send any Sudama Soul Cores dropped by merchants to your item box. This happens from the second one onwards, which means you won’t have to pick half a dozen each time you go to sell a batch of items.

Speaking of the item box, the limit of forging materials has been increased for some of them. If you’ve been running Battle Scroll missions and Expeditions for gear, you’ll be happy to know that you can now exit the session from the main menu directly.

There’s plenty more to patch 1.04, including fixes and balance tweaks for several weapons, such as Samurai dual swords, odachi, and more for a few Ninja weapons, too. The patch also brings several bug fixes to the game.

You can read the full set of patch notes on Steam.

#4284. You Can Preload Grand Theft Auto VI On PS5 and Xbox Next Week, And You'll Want To Because It's Massive

We're just over two weeks away from the launch of Grand Theft Auto VI, which recently graced the cover of Game Informer. Ahead of its November 19 launch, Rockstar Games has announced that digital preloading for GTA VI will begin next week on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S.

More specifically, preloading on Xbox Series X/S will begin Tuesday, November 10, at 12 a.m. GMT (4 p.m. PT/7 p.m. ET on November 9), and on PS5 at midnight local time in your time zone. Although Rockstar isn't producing physical discs of GTA VI, you can still buy a physical box at retail, which includes a download code for the game. The studio says, "Code-in-box versions for both consoles should be available from retailers beginning November 12."

The preload file will require 212 GB on your device, so make sure you have the space before you start the download. You can find more details about this process here.

#4283. Tekken, Marvel Vs Capcom, And SoulCalibur Are Now Available In-Browser

Sam Woods is TheGamer’s Senior Reporter. He’s been in games journalism since 2020 and has undertaken a variety of roles in that time. These have included roles such as SEO Editor, Managing Editor at DualShockers, and Global Head of Gaming, and he's also been seen on the BBC. He was promoted to the Senior Reporter position in 2025 following a series of high-quality reports and exclusives for TheGamer.

Since 2020, Sam has written over 3,000 articles and specializes in telling the stories of the people behind the games. He’s interviewed the biggest game directors, some of the industry’s top talents, told the stories of how indie games came to be, and spoken to players about what really makes them tick. He’s also interviewed some of the world’s biggest musical artists to find out how the medium has inspired their work, and TV and Film actors about their roles in video game adaptations. He even hosted a PAX panel in 2021 and made a documentary in 2024 surrounding the creation of a Disney game.

Alongside this, Sam focuses on breaking news. He got the scoop on Perfect Dark’s cancellation, provided context on some AI drama, and revealed that Lady Dimitrescu’s actress would love to step back into the character’s giant shoes. These articles have been picked up by the biggest gaming sites, including IGN, GameSpot, and PC Gamer. He also loves to dive into the numbers behind the games.

Sam’s journey in games journalism has taken him all over the world. He’s covered Gamescom in Germany, Summer Game Fest in Los Angeles, and Tokyo Game Show in Japan, each on three occasions.

He’s been learning Japanese since 2024 with the intention of identifying and translating Japanese-language news and bringing it to English-language audiences first, something he’s done countless times.

Sam’s first review was 2020’s Battletoads reboot, and he’s since reviewed games in The Legend of Zelda, Super Mario, and Pokemon franchises.

For many, the PlayStation 2 has the greatest library of games of any console. It had some of the best entries from series like Grand Theft Auto, God of War, Resident Evil, and Metal Gear Solid. It also birthed classics like Okami, Shadow of the Colossus, and Ico.

In a time when couch co-op was king, the PS2 also had a phenomenal selection of fighting games, with Tekken and SoulCalibur reigning supreme. And as a wave of video games make their way from older consoles to web browsers, the PlayStation 2's fighting game collection has become a focus, with four of them now playable on the internet.

Recent advances in web emulation and generative AI have let gamers run complex sixth-generation console games directly in modern browsers. We've seen multiple examples in the past weeks, including Need for Speed: Underground 2 and Dragon Ball Z: Budokai, and now more PS2-era games have made their way online.

The first in-browser title is Tekken 4. It's the fifth game in the Tekken franchise, coming after 1999's Tekken Tag Tournament, and the first developed specifically for the PlayStation 2. It featured 23 fighters and a full story mode that unlocked character-specific cutscenes. It was a staple in couch co-op gaming.

SoulCalibur 2 now also has a browser version. While not rated as highly as its predecessor, which is the second-best game ever created according to Metacritic, it's easily one of the most impressive traditional 1v1 fighters. Its array of vastly different characters was supplemented on each platform by an exclusive fighter, with Link appearing in the GameCube version, Spawn in the Xbox version, and Tekken's Heihachi Mishima in the PlayStation version. It's certainly the game on this list I have the fondest memories of.

Marvel Vs. Capcom 2 is next up and has arguably the most impressive roster of fighters from any fighting game in that era. 56 characters from across Marvel and Capcom duke it out in the fighter that scored a 76 on Metacritic.

The final game is Street Fighter Anniversary Collection. This title featured both Hyper Street Fighter 2 and Street Fighter 3 3rd Strike in one nifty package. It was arguably the best way to play any Street Fighter game on Sony's second home console.

If you choose to hunt these down, be careful. They carry a legal risk if you play copyrighted games without owning a copy, and many are laden with intrusive ads that could download malware or other dangerous programs to your devices.

We want to hear from you. Share your perspective in the comments below, and please keep the conversation respectful.

#4282. The Ratchet & Clank Game You Didn’t Know Existed is Shutting Down

Daniel is a lifelong gamer with a love for various genres and gameplay styles who enjoys exploring games and playing from various angles.

I’ll admit, I have a tendency to hyperfixate on games and franchises that I care about, occasionally to the detriment of others. Even so, I like to consider myself sufficiently plugged-into this industry, especially when it comes to relatively big-name IPs like the Ratchet & Clank series. You can imagine my distinct confusion, then, when I heard today that Ratchet & Clank: Ranger Rumble was shutting down, to which my response was, “what the heck is Ratchet & Clank: Ranger Rumble?”

Apparently it is, soon to be “was,” a PvP live service shooter available for iOS and Android. The game saw a soft-launch in mid-2025 in limited territories like Canada, France, and parts of Asia, which probably explains why I have literally never heard of it alongside the fact that I don’t often pay much mind to mobile games in general.

In the wake of Destiny 2's upcoming final content update, thousands of of fans have called for Destiny 3 to begin development.

What’s especially interesting about this particular discontinuation, however, is that the game wasn’t even actually finished yet. That soft-launch was as far as the game had ever managed to get, with its planned global launch officially being scrapped and further development ceasing as of the game’s most recent update today, according to its official home page.

As the home page announcement explains, with the newest update pushed out today to mobile storefronts, no further updates for Ratchet & Clank: Ranger Rumble will be released, and on November 21, the game will be pulled from said storefronts entirely.

This is a feature that looks at how live service games are dying as a popular choice in the industry.

For those who are still actively playing the game, you don’t have to stop playing it right away. While new players won’t be able to download the game from the Google Play or Apple App stores anymore following the delisting, anyone who already has the game downloaded will be able to keep playing multiplayer matches until the servers are officially closed in May 2027.

On November 21, the game will be pulled from storefronts entirely.

The game’s “Qwark Pass” seasons will continue running until the server closure, while the game’s “Super Pass” has been made free, with all of its related content now available to earn throughout the remaining seasons. Of course, said content will vanish into the ether once the game goes offline, so whether or not you can be bothered is up to you.

This also goes for any in-app purchases made on things like currency, cosmetics, upgrades, and so forth. If you’re looking to get a refund for any of that, the developers suggest you contact the Apple App Store and Google Play Store’s respective support lines to determine eligibility. Again, absolutely everything is being erased when the servers shutter in May, so whether you want a refund or to keep playing, you’d better act now.

In its final announcement, the developers offered some words of thanks to the players who joined them for the soft-launch process. “On behalf of the dev team and everyone helping to make the game, thanks to our amazing community for all your support, especially to those who have spent time playing, sharing feedback, and helping shape Ranger Rumble throughout its development,” they wrote.

While not as high-profile as some other historic live-service flops over the years, the discontinuation of Ratchet & Clank: Ranger Rumble is another good sign that live-service games are reaching the end of an era. Aside from a very fortunate few that manage to keep attention with consistent updates and player-grabbing content like Fortnite’s One Piece event, the majority end up crashing and burning well before they can take off in earnest.

Sony in particular has been putting the kibosh on live-service games left and right for the last couple of years, mostly following the disastrous launch of Concord, and it seems even its major first-party PlayStation IPs like Ratchet & Clank aren’t safe from the proverbial axe.

Sony Interactive Entertainment executive Hideaki Nishino doubles down on multiplayer investments during a recent Famitsu interview.

#4281. The Sims 4 patch makes it so your public lot gatherings won't be interrupted by rogue Sims

Stranger Sims will no longer just crash your public lot events in The Sims 4 to talk about whatever.

The Sims 4 will soon get a new update to resolve a number of issues, some of which have long caused headaches for players. The latest update will arrive March 17 on PC and Mac, followed by PlayStation and Xbox at an unspecified time later.

Outside of the fixes themselves, the patch also makes good on the recent re-commitment to continue improving quality of life for players, so there’s plenty here longtime players will appreciate.

In the latest episode of The Sims 4’s Laundry List blog series, where the developer goes through the most reported problems with the game and how it plans to solve them, we got a rundown of what to expect from next week’s patch.

You can look forward to five major fixes in this one, but arguably the most important is a change to how Sims determine who they speak with on a lot. This is especially relevant for public lots, where Sims would sometimes interrupt ongoing conversations by barging in and starting a conversation with your Sim.

Going forward, Sims will prioritise familiar Sims with whom they already have rapport, and be less likely to latch onto strangers. If you’ve witnessed a date your Sim was on get interrupted because of that, you’ll certainly appreciate the change.

Speaking of budding romance, Prom is coming back to in-game Calendars, and Sims can once again attend. Maxis said this will work with new and existing saves, and that you should also expect Prom goals to be completable once again.

Pets and animals get some love in this patch, too. First, pets and horses will no longer get lost in Premade Households. The fix prevents that from happening in new saves, but if you already had that happen to you in your current save, it’ll still be there.

You may now also assign animals to an Animal Shed after moving your house to a new lot, so you hopefully won’t be confused as to why they’re stuck in your inventory. This fix applies to existing saves as well as new ones.

Lower down the list of urgent fixes is an update that makes it so Sims’ eye blinking will show fully closed eyes for most interactions. The upcoming patch also comes with a host of Sims autonomy fixes, including one that prevents them from excessively flirting with each other.

Catch up on the full list at the link near the top of the page. And, in case you missed it, Maxis recently announced that The Sims 4 will soon get paid mods, something that many in the community are skeptical about.
